head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: All 41 manifest files read in full; no partners. Many style hits in this chunk are already carried by the known ledger (peekID naming/order, LoadFragment duplication, RunSync duplication, policy.go literals/ordering, bootstrap_darwin conditions, etc.) and were not re-reported. Cross-chunk suspicions for the station: (1) NIT-4's third copy of the agent branch prefixes lives in internal/server/repos.go:537 (other chunk); (2) internal/server/config_sync_test.go repeats the "install.env" literal next to NIT-2; (3) RunResult.IsRunning (routines.go:125) shares its name with the package-level IsRunning(ctx, label) launchd/Task-Scheduler probe — a naming judgement, not raised as a claim.

findings.fix: Declare the peek control port default once (e.g. config.DefaultPeekControlPort as an int const) and use it for the -peek-control-port flag default in cmd/configserver/main.go:52, formatting it with strconv.Itoa in installEnvValues.
findings.claim: The new exported constant DefaultPeekControlPort = "42442" restates the -peek-control-port flag default 42442 hard-coded in cmd/configserver/main.go:52; the two defaults are independent declarations of one value. Changing the flag default alone (the server then spawns peek with the new control port when install.env is absent) leaves ExpandInstallMarkers expanding {{PEEK_CONTROL_PORT}} in repo fragments to the old 42442, so fragment-vs-live comparison reports drift for an install that never wrote install.env.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/config/installenv.go:8-12,24-29 at the head and cmd/configserver/main.go:52; git grep at 1f725ce for DefaultPeekControlPort and 42442 over *.go shows the const is used only at installenv.go:25 and the int literal 42442 appears separately at main.go:52 — no shared declaration links them. Not in the known ledger (the ledger's installenv.go:20 row is about the PEEK_CONTROL_PORT key literal, not the default value).

findings.fix: Export the file name from internal/config (e.g. config.InstallEnvFile = "install.env") and use it in writeInstallEnv instead of the bare "install.env" literal.
findings.claim: writeInstallEnv writes the per-install env file under its own bare literal "install.env" while its only Go reader, config.ExpandInstallMarkers, resolves the same file through the unexported constant installEnvPath = "install.env" (installenv.go:11). Writer and reader spell the file-name contract separately, so renaming the constant (the reader) silently leaves the Windows installer writing a file nothing reads and fragments expanding to the default port.
findings.evidence: Re-read install_windows.go:136-149 and installenv.go:8-22 at the head; git grep for "install.env" over *.go at 1f725ce shows the literal at install_windows.go:145 and the constant at installenv.go:11 with no cross-reference (the remaining hits are test files). Not a variant of any known-ledger row.

findings.fix: Extract one sessionFromItem(item listItem) Session constructor (Cwd cleaned, GitBranch, Live) and call it from both SessionIndex and SessionsById.
findings.claim: SessionIndex (peek.go:109-116) and SessionsById (peek.go:144-150) each build a Session from a listItem field by field; the change added GitBranch to the SessionIndex copy only, so the two mappings have already diverged — SessionsById returns GitBranch "" for a session whose meta carries git_branch "claude/feature", while SessionIndex returns "claude/feature" for the same item.
findings.evidence: Re-read peek.go:92-153 at the head: the SessionIndex literal sets GitBranch: item.Meta.GitBranch, the SessionsById literal (unchanged by the diff) sets Id, Cwd, LastActive, Live, Title only. git grep at 1f725ce shows no current reader of GitBranch on SessionsById results (internal/server/welcome.go:190,383 use it), hence exposure eventually.

findings.fix: Pass the agent branch prefixes into Fingerprint (or declare them once in package repos, e.g. AgentBranchPrefixes, used by Fingerprint, WorktreeCounts callers and ops.go) instead of hard-coding refs/heads/claude/ and refs/heads/claude-routines/.
findings.claim: Fingerprint hard-codes the agent branch prefix set (refs/heads/claude/, refs/heads/claude-routines/) while the sibling WorktreeCounts added in the same change takes that set as a parameter, supplied by internal/server/repos.go:537 (and spelled a third time in internal/repos/ops.go:118). Adding a prefix to the server's list makes WorktreeCounts count that prefix's worktrees while Fingerprint ignores its branch tips, so the status cache keyed on Fingerprint serves a stale entry after such a branch moves.
findings.evidence: Re-read registry.go:453-508 at the head; git grep at 1f725ce for WorktreeCounts(, Fingerprint( and the prefix literals shows server/repos.go:537 branchPrefixes := []string{"claude/", "claude-routines/"} feeding WorktreeCounts, ops.go:118 its own literal pair, and registry.go:458 the third copy. Known-ledger rows on registry.go:458 concern call layout (single-line 7-arg shell.Run), not this duplication.
